title: Origins and Road to War
sub: How the Estonian War of Independence began

slides.title: From Russian Civil War to Estonian War of Independence
slides.cap: Historical connection: Imperial collapse and Baltic independence
slides.body: The Russian Civil War created both the opportunity and the danger for Estonian independence. Estonia declared sovereignty as empires collapsed, but then had to defeat a Bolshevik attempt to restore control.

slides.title: Before the Estonian War of Independence
slides.body:
Estonia declared independence as the German occupation ended, but the Red Army invaded to restore Bolshevik control over the former Russian imperial province.

The Conflict Takes Shape: The young republic fought for national survival against Soviet forces and later against German-led Landeswehr formations. The opening phase established the political goals, alliances, and military problems that shaped every later campaign.

title: Battle of Narva
sub: Part of Estonian War of Independence

slides.title: Battle of Narva
slides.body:
The Battle of Narva took place on 29 November 1918 in the city of Narva and Jaanilinn between troops from the Provisional Government of Estonia and the Russian Red Army. The battle is considered the beginning of the Estonian Independence War. The Infanterie-Regiment Nr. 405 of the German Imperial Army was also involved against the Red Army.

Why This Moment Matters: Battle of Narva was more than an isolated engagement. It helped define the conflict's direction and exposed the strengths and weaknesses of the opposing sides. The young republic fought for national survival against Soviet forces and later against German-led Landeswehr formations.

Consequences: The effects of Battle of Narva extended beyond its immediate result. Mobilization and shifting fronts placed severe pressure on a small population already exhausted by world war and occupation. Its place in the wider campaign also influenced later military choices and political calculations.

title: Battle of Tartu
sub: Part of Estonian War of Independence

slides.title: Battle of Tartu
slides.body:
The Battle of Tartu was fought between the 13th and 14th of January, 1919 in the Estonian War of Independence between the units of the Estonian 2nd Division and the forces of the Red Latvian Riflemen. The battle was a significant battle in the Estonian War of Independence, allowing Estonian troops to liberate the rest of Southern Estonia from Soviet forces.

slides.title: Battle of Utria
slides.body:
Battle of Utria also known as the Utria Landing took place during the Estonian War of Independence on 17–20 January 1919 at Udria beach. It was an amphibious landing consisting mainly of Finnish volunteers.

sub: Part of Estonian War of Independence

slides.title: Battle of Laagna
slides.body:
Battle of Laagna took place in Laagna, Estonia, during the Estonian War of Independence. A battalion of Estonian marines and four companies of Finnish volunteers under the overall command of Martin Ekström attacked Red Army positions at Laagna as part of a wider operation targeting Narva.

title: Battle of Paju
sub: Part of Estonian War of Independence

slides.title: Battle of Paju
slides.body:
The Battle of Paju was fought in Paju, near Valga, Estonia, on 31 January 1919 during the Estonian War of Independence. After heavy fighting, the Tartu-Valga group of the Estonian Army pushed the Red Latvian Riflemen out of the Paju Manor. It was the fiercest battle in the early period of war. Estonian commander Julius Kuperjanov fell in the fighting.

Why This Moment Matters: Battle of Paju was more than an isolated engagement. It reflected the changing balance of power and pushed the conflict closer to its eventual outcome. The young republic fought for national survival against Soviet forces and later against German-led Landeswehr formations.

Consequences: The effects of Battle of Paju extended beyond its immediate result. title: Battle of Cēsis
sub: Part of Estonian War of Independence

slides.title: Battle of Cēsis
slides.body:
The Battle of Cēsis, fought near Cēsis (Wenden) in June 1919, was a decisive battle in the Estonian War of Independence and the Latvian War of Independence. After heavy fighting, an Estonian force moving from the north, supplemented by Latvian units, repelled Baltic German attacks and went on a full counter-attack.

Why This Moment Matters: Battle of Cēsis was more than an isolated engagement. It reflected the changing balance of power and pushed the conflict closer to its eventual outcome. The young republic fought for national survival against Soviet forces and later against German-led Landeswehr formations.

sub: Part of Estonian War of Independence

slides.title: Battle of Krivasoo
slides.body:
Battle of Krivasoo took place near the Krivasoo, Estonia during the Estonian War of Independence between the Estonian Army and the Red Army. It is considered one of the last engagements of the conflict before a ceasefire was called in early January 1920.

title: International and Human Dimensions
sub: The wider impact of the Estonian War of Independence

slides.title: International Dimension
slides.body:
British naval support, Finnish volunteers, White Russian forces, and fighting in neighboring Latvia affected Estonia's ability to survive.

title: Outcome and Legacy
sub: How the Estonian War of Independence ended and what followed

slides.title: The End of the Estonian War of Independence
slides.body: Estonian forces secured the country, and Soviet Russia recognized Estonian independence in the Treaty of Tartu.
